desc: Kona Blue was a Department of Homeland Security prospective special access programme, terminated on 10 February 2012, intended to house UAP recovery and reverse-engineering work after the DIA's AAWSAP/AATIP funding lapsed. AARO surfaced it in the Historical Record Report Volume I and DHS declassified the associated records; on 5 February 2024 DHS Acting Deputy Secretary Kristie Canegallo transmitted them to the Deputy Secretary of Defense, with strike-through formatting preserving the former classification marks and a records search finding no further material. The documents were made public in June 2024. AARO's framing is that Kona Blue was rejected by DHS leadership as lacking merit and that it is the proximate origin of the modern belief in a crash-retrieval programme - people who saw the Kona Blue proposal, on this account, mistook a proposal for an existing capability. The record is more interesting than the framing. A prospective special access programme is a real, chartered vehicle, and the surviving text discusses protection rationales for sensitive personnel and exotic technologies. The federal government did not draft a SAP charter to house nothing; it drafted one because named officials with clearances believed there was something to house, and the charter reached the Acting Deputy Secretary level of DHS before it was killed. AARO uses Kona Blue as a debunking device; on its face it is documentary evidence that in 2011-2012 senior officials at two departments treated recovered exotic material as a programme-management problem.

connections: Direct successor to the DIA AAWSAP/AATIP contract; the same declassification package contains the Reid-Lynn letter and the Burgess memo recommending transition to another agency.

Tara O'Toole (DHS U/S S&T, formerly of the UPMC Center for Biosecurity) is the establishing authority and the person who briefed Reid and Lieberman. She is the pivot between the Senate and the DHS compartment.
Jane Holl Lute (DHS Deputy Secretary, former UN Assistant Secretary-General) is the killer of record. Her stated reason is documentary insufficiency, not falsity of the underlying claims.
Joseph Lieberman as HSGAC chairman is the second Senate sponsor alongside Reid, a linkage that does not appear in the AATIP-era documents.

Steven J. Cover (DHS SAPCO), Ivan Fong (DHS General Counsel), Caryn Wagner (U/S I&A), Rafael Borras (U/S Management), Gregory Marshall (CSO), Joel Wall (S&T SPO), and Associate General Counsel Kronisch are all named participants with living memory of the program.
The 'body of previous work held by other entities' language is the single most connectable phrase in the file; it implies at least one SAP-protected holder outside DHS and DIA.
The 'Consciousness Center' research line ties KONA BLUE back to the BAASS/Skinwalker work stream and forward to human-effects claims made in later congressional testimony.
AARO Director Sean Kirkpatrick publicly attributed whistleblower crash-retrieval claims to KONA BLUE, making the program the government's preferred explanation for those claims.
dossier.denialPosture: AARO's position, published as the cover narrative to the 2024 release, is that KONA BLUE 'was a Prospective Special Access Program (PSAP) that had been proposed to DHS leadership but was never approved or formally established,' that it 'never received any materials or funding,' and that 'there is no information beyond the proposal presentation marked with the KONA BLUE name.' The DHS paperwork it accompanies contradicts the 'never established' framing on its face: O'Toole did establish it as a PSAP on 11 July 2011 and Lute had to formally terminate it. AARO's denial is scoped to SAP approval and to DHS custody, not to the existence of the material claims that motivated the proposal.
dossier.narrative:
The declassified package released jointly by DoD and DHS is unusually complete: an establishment memo, a decision briefing, SAPOC minutes, an action memo, a termination memo, a memorandum for the record, and — folded into the same release — the underlying Reid letter and DIA info memo that explain where the program came from.

Establishment: on 11 July 2011 the Director of DHS S&T's Special Projects Office asked Dr. Tara O'Toole, Under Secretary for Science and Technology and an Original Classification Authority, to approve creation of KONA BLUE as a Prospective Special Access Program under DHS Instruction 140-04-001. The stated purpose was "to investigate, identify and analyze sensitive advanced materials and technologies and to assess potential emerging and/or disruptive scientific and technical data necessary in support of national security." O'Toole approved. Classification was TOP SECRET//KONA BLUE//NOFORN, HANDLE VIA SPECIAL ACCESS CHANNELS ONLY, classified under E.O. reason 1.4(e), with a declassification date of 25 April 2036. The DHS SAPCO decision briefing lists the program manager as Joel Wall, S&T Special Programs Division.

Scope: the proposal document describes four research centers — Data Collection and Analysis, Advanced Technology, Consciousness, and Technology Application/Integration — investigating "emerging and/or disruptive advanced materials and controls, alternative energy/power source/generation opportunities, temporal translation; human effects and interface, signature reduction and weaponry, as well as technology integration." That is the AAWSAP twelve-area list with a Consciousness Center bolted on. The Department's interest area is stated as "the scientific and technical investigation, threat analysis, and assessment of materials and data of unique origin, engineering, and purpose." Materials of unique origin. Written by DHS.

Money: the planned research objectives slide gives FY12 $12M, FY13 $25M, FY14 $35-50M, FY15-FY18 TBD. The SAPCO briefing gives "Expected amount for funding expected to be 12 to 15m" and flags a pending issue: a "Classified Line Item in CSO budget" and that the Under Secretary for Management "has concurred in the need to establish a Business/Administrative SAP to handle primarily 'unacknowledged' monies (e.g., KONA BLUE)." A dedicated financial vehicle for unacknowledged money was being stood up to receive it.

The politics are in the SAPOC minutes of 21 November 2011, chaired by Deputy Secretary Jane Holl Lute, with Caryn Wagner (U/S Intelligence and Analysis), Rafael Borras (U/S Management), Ivan Fong (General Counsel), Gregory Marshall (Chief Security Officer), Steven J. Cover (Chief SAPCO), security officers Michael Zawasky and Allen Olsen, and O'Toole. The minutes record that "The Deputy Secretary opened the meeting with an explanation of what caused this meeting to occur with some sense of urgency which was the impending transfer of funds to DHS from Senators Reid and Leiberman to conduct the KONA BLUE program." O'Toole "stated that the Senators were prepared to provide $10M for the execution of this program in the FY12 budget." She was asked why the FBI was not approached and answered that the FBI "had no organic capability to do research & development in the scientific arena." Wagner raised whether S&T even had collection authority, and whether KONA BLUE "is actually an intelligence program which DIA no longer had the authority to conduct per Executive Order 12333." Lute closed by tasking O'Toole and Cover with a 5-10 page paper documenting "how we got to where we are now with the KONA BLUE program, it's provenance (history) while at DIA, and exactly what science would be researched," adding that "S2 is still not certain of what the 'It' is in the program or otherwise what exactly we are researching."

The November action memo from O'Toole records that in October 2011 she met with Senator Lieberman, Chairman of Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, and Senate Majority Leader Reid, to discuss program funding. It also states the operative custody claim: "A SAP is proposed as we have been informed that there is a body of previous work held by other entities that requires a SAP level classification to access it."

Death: a progress review was held 8 December 2011 in Lute's office with Fong, Wagner, Cover and Associate General Counsel Kronisch. O'Toole was invited but could not attend. Lute directed immediate termination. The termination memo is dated 12 December 2011 and Lute's signature block shows Disapprove dated 2-10-12. DHS's Acting Deputy Secretary Kristie Canegallo confirmed in a 5 February 2024 letter to Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen Hicks that the PSAP was "terminated on February 10, 2012." A memorandum for the record from Cover dated 5 June 2013 states that no security classification guide, SOP, facility accreditation or AIS plan was ever issued, that all briefed personnel would be administratively debriefed, and that "No other documentation or paperwork would be required."

AARO's framing, published in 2024, is that KONA BLUE "never received any materials or funding" and that "no data or material of any kind was ever transferred to or collected by DHS under the auspices of KONA BLUE." On the narrow question of DHS custody, the paperwork supports that. On the broader question the AARO narrative raises and does not answer: DHS believed material would be delivered, and DHS wrote that a body of prior work was held by other entities under SAP protection. AARO does not identify those entities.
openQuestions: Which 'other entities' held the SAP-level body of previous work referenced in O'Toole's 28 November 2011 memo? The released record never names them.
The 5-10 page provenance paper Lute tasked O'Toole and Cover to produce has not been released. Was it written?
The redacted General Counsel remarks in the SAPOC minutes on the rationale for SAP status are the only substantive redaction in the minutes. What did Fong say?
Was the $10M FY12 congressional add ever appropriated, and if so where did it go after termination on 10 February 2012?
Who were the individuals administratively debriefed on 5 June 2013, seventeen months after termination, and why the delay?

AARO says there is 'no information beyond the proposal presentation marked with the KONA BLUE name.' Enclosures 1 through 4 to the O'Toole action memo are referenced but not all released. Where are they?
dossier.whatItIs: KONA BLUE was an unacknowledged, waived Prospective Special Access Program established inside the Department of Homeland Security Science and Technology Directorate by Under Secretary Dr. Tara O'Toole on 11 July 2011, and terminated by Deputy Secretary Jane Holl Lute effective 10 February 2012. Its stated purpose was "to investigate, identify and potentially exploit sensitive advanced aerospace-related technology and to prevent disclosure of scientific, technical and engineering data vital to the US." It was the direct successor proposal to the DIA AAWSAP/AATIP contract and was to be funded by a congressional add steered by Senators Reid and Lieberman.
dossier.whyImplicated: KONA BLUE is the best-documented attempt in the modern record to build a compartmented U.S. government home for exploitation of materials of claimed non-human origin, and the government declassified the paperwork itself in 2023-2024. The program's own approval memo states DHS proposed a SAP because "we have been informed that there is a body of previous work held by other entities that requires a SAP level classification to access it." That sentence is an admission, in a signed DHS action memo, that someone told the Under Secretary for Science and Technology that SAP-protected prior work existed and was held elsewhere. AARO's cover narrative asserts that interviewees identified KONA BLUE as "a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) sensitive compartment established to protect the retrieval and exploitation of 'non-human biologics'" and then argues the program never got materials because it was never approved. Both can be true and the interesting question survives: who were the "other entities," and what was the "body of previous work"? The termination reason of record is not that the claims were false. Deputy Secretary Lute killed it over adequacy of threat/vulnerability justification and insufficiency of budget and personnel documentation.

timeline.label: KONA BLUE proposed to DHS
timeline.text: AAWSAP's advocates propose a prospective special access program at DHS to restart the work and reverse-engineer any recovered craft they hoped to acquire. DHS rejects it. AARO notes it was never reported to Congress because it never met the SAP threshold.

timeline.label: KONA BLUE proposed at DHS
timeline.text: A successor special access program to house UAP recovery and reverse-engineering work is proposed to the Department of Homeland Security and subsequently rejected by DHS leadership.

timeline.label: AARO and DHS publish the KONA BLUE history
timeline.text: The joint paper confirms that a DHS component head established a prospective special access program in 2011 and that the Deputy Secretary killed it six months later.

timeline.label: Kona Blue documents made public
